title: The German engineers who spoke English at the Unbroken session
summary: The German promoter said the engineers could not speak English, but they stopped a take for a squeaking horn.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You know, I got to tell you something about this. When we went there, we had this German promoter and he did all the translating. He says, "Now, all of these fellas are Germans and they don't speak any English. But they all are finished concert pianists." So if you notice, they love piano. You know how many records they got of Oscar Peterson. And they are good piano players. He said, "They're hip music-wise, but they can't talk." So he says, "I'll do all the translating." We say, "Okay." So we were going (HUMMING) and Ben's horn had rubber bands on it because they torn it up on the plane, as I said before. So after we'd gone over it about three or four times, without his horn -- his horn would squeak every time. But after we got one through -- we didn't hear it squeak, but one of the guys heard it in the control room. So now they ain't said nothing all day, you
know, just -- so when we get through and we run through it, he say, "Wait a minute, wait a minute." It was such a surprise. Everybody says, "I thought he couldn't talk."

"We can't let that through." So I says, "You've been jiving all day," you know what I mean? That was a joke, you know, and it cracked up everybody, even them. They fell out in the control rooms. So they said, "Well, I'm going to bring everybody a drink down --" So that was on this "Unbroken."
